newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Marchelli says franc-mark link sterile-paper.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Marchelli says franc-mark link sterile-paper.

text.p: Paul Marchelli, a member of the Bank of France's monetary policy council, was quoted on Tuesday as saying the link between the franc and the mark was sterile.
"The franc-mark link is sterile because it forces us to wait for the Bundesbank to lower its interest rates before we can lower ours," daily Liberation quoted him as saying.

Marchelli, who is believed to be outnumbered on the monetary policy council by those who defend the franc-mark link, said that "we should do everything to lower our interest rates as quickly as possible, which will allow an acceleration in growth and (the franc) to find a suitable level against the dollar".
His comments are likely to stoke a debate started last week when former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing called in a magazine article for a sharp depreciation in the franc.

Marchelli defended the monetary policy council, installed in 1994 when the Bank became independent, as an institution, but said that if the government wanted a different monetary policy, it should have "named different men".
The paper said that out of the nine members of the monetary policy council, six supported the current policy of defending the franc-mark link.
These included governor Jean-Claude Trichet, deputy governors Herve Hannoun and Denis Ferman, and lay members Jean Boissonat, Michel Albert and Bruno de Maulde.
The mandates of both Boissonat and de Maulde expire at the end of this year although their terms of office are renewable.
The presidents of the upper and lower houses of parliament and of the Economic and Social Council are due to nominate six people for the posts coming up, out of which the government will choose two.
The newspaper said those opposed to the current policy were Marchelli, Jean-Pierre Gerard and Denise Flouzat.
Marchelli's comments were the first time a member of the secretive monetary policy council had publicly criticised the Bank's policies.
